subject: maths
title: Roman Numerals to 100
seo_title: Year 4 Roman Numerals Worksheets (I to C): Free Maths Practice with Answer Key
standard_text: Read Roman numerals to 100 (I to C) and know that over time, the numeral system changed to include the concept of zero and place value.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 Roman numerals worksheets for the National Curriculum: I, V, X, L and C, the subtraction rule (IV, IX, XL, XC), reading and writing numbers to 100, clocks, kings and queens, and why the Romans had no zero. 100 questions with answer key.
key_big: Add when the same or a smaller symbol comes after. Take away when a smaller symbol comes before: IV = 4, IX = 9, XL = 40, XC = 90.
key_sub: I = 1, V = 5, X = 10, L = 50, C = 100. Partition into tens and ones: 47 = XL + VII = XLVII. Never write 4 of the same symbol in a row.
body_html:
Five symbols

Roman numerals use letters for numbers. To 100 you need only five of them.

Add or take away?

  1. Same or smaller symbol after: add. VI = 5 + 1 = 6. LX = 50 + 10 = 60.
  2. Smaller symbol before a bigger one: take it away. IV = 5 − 1 = 4. XL = 50 − 10 = 40.
  3. Never more than 3 of the same symbol in a row. 4 is IV, not IIII. 40 is XL, not XXXX.
Take awayMeansValue
IV5 − 14
IX10 − 19
XL50 − 1040
XC100 − 1090

These four pairs are the only ones you need to 100. I goes only before V or X, and X goes only before L or C.

Read a Roman numeral

Split it into tens and ones, then add.

Read

What number is LXXXIX?

Tens: LXXX = 50 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 80. Ones: IX = 10 − 1 = 9. 80 + 9 = 89.

Answer: 89

Write a number as a Roman numeral

Partition the number into tens and ones. Write the tens, then the ones.

Tens102030405060708090100
RomanXXXXXXXLLLXLXXLXXXXCC
Ones123456789
RomanIIIIIIIVVVIVIIVIIIIX
Write

Write 49 in Roman numerals.

49 = 40 + 9. 40 = XL and 9 = IX. Put them together.

Answer: XLIX (not IL)

Roman numerals in real life

You see them on clock faces, after the names of kings and queens (Henry VIII, Elizabeth II), on chapters of books and in the titles of films.

No zero and no place value

In our number 77, the first 7 is worth 70 and the second 7 is worth 7: the place changes the value. In Roman numerals, X always means 10, wherever it is. That is why the Romans did not need a zero. Our digits 0 to 9, with zero and place value, came later from India through Arabic mathematicians. They make big numbers and written calculations much easier.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
IIII for 4, XXXX for 40Never 4 of the same symbol in a row: IV, XL
Adding every symbol (IX = 11, XL = 60)Smaller before bigger means take away: IX = 9, XL = 40
IL for 49, IC for 99Partition first: 49 = XL + IX = XLIX, 99 = XC + IX = XCIX
VX for 5, LC for 50V and L are never put before a bigger symbol: 5 = V, 50 = L
Writing 47 as IVVII (4 then 7)40 is XL, not IV: 47 = XLVII

faq.q: Do Year 4 children need to learn Roman numerals?
faq.a: Yes. The National Curriculum in England says Year 4 pupils should read Roman numerals to 100 (I to C) and know that the number system changed over time to include zero and place value.

faq.q: How do you write 4 and 9 in Roman numerals?
faq.a: 4 is IV (5 − 1) and 9 is IX (10 − 1). A smaller symbol before a bigger one is taken away, so you never write IIII or VIIII.

faq.q: Why do some clocks show IIII instead of IV?
faq.a: Many clockmakers use IIII as a tradition, partly so the face looks balanced opposite VIII. In maths, the correct way to write 4 is IV.

faq.q: Why did the Romans not have a zero?
faq.a: Each Roman symbol always has the same value, so there are no empty places to fill. Zero is only needed with place value, which came to Europe later from India through Arabic mathematicians.

sets.title: The symbols I, V, X, L, C and numbers to 20

items.e: I means 1.
V means 5. Do not mix it up with X, which means 10.
X means 10.
L means 50. Do not mix it up with C, which means 100.
C means 100. C is the first letter of the Latin word centum, which means a hundred (think of a century).
5 has its own symbol: V. VX is not a Roman numeral: V is never put before a bigger symbol. IIIII uses 5 Is, but you never write more than 3 of the same symbol in a row.
III = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. It is not 111: each I means 1, wherever it is.
Split it into tens and ones: X = 10 and II = 1 + 1 = 2. So XII = 10 + 2 = 12.
Split it into tens and ones: X = 10 and V = 5. So XV = 10 + 5 = 15.
Split it into tens and ones: X = 10 and I = 1. So XI = 10 + 1 = 11.
Split it into tens and ones: X = 10 and VIII = 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 8. So XVIII = 10 + 8 = 18.
Split it into tens and ones: X = 10 and VII = 5 + 1 + 1 = 7. So XVII = 10 + 7 = 17.
6 = 5 + 1, so 6 = VI. IV is 4, because the I comes before the V.
8 = 5 + 1 + 1 + 1, so 8 = VIII. IIX is wrong: you can only put one I before a bigger symbol.
Partition 12 into 10 + 2. 10 is X and 2 is II. So 12 = XII. III is only 3: the 1 ten must be written X.
Partition 13 into 10 + 3. 10 is X and 3 is III. So 13 = XIII.
Partition 16 into 10 + 6. 10 is X and 6 is VI. So 16 = XVI.

sets.title: The subtraction rule: IV, IX, XL and XC

items.e: IV = 5 − 1 = 4. A smaller symbol before a bigger one is taken away, so IV is not 6.
IX = 10 − 1 = 9. A smaller symbol before a bigger one is taken away, so IX is not 11.
Split it into tens and ones: X = 10 and IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So XIV = 10 + 4 = 14. The I comes before the bigger symbol, so take it away. XIV is not 16.
Split it into tens and ones: X = 10 and IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So XIX = 10 + 9 = 19. The I comes before the bigger symbol, so take it away. XIX is not 21.
XL = 50 − 10 = 40. A smaller symbol before a bigger one is taken away, so XL is not 60.
XC = 100 − 10 = 90. A smaller symbol before a bigger one is taken away, so XC is not 110.
50 has its own symbol: L. LC is not allowed: L is never put before a bigger symbol. C is 100, and XXXXX uses too many Xs.
Split it into tens and ones: XX = 10 + 10 = 20 and IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So XXIV = 20 + 4 = 24.
Split it into tens and ones: XXX = 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 and VII = 5 + 1 + 1 = 7. So XXXVII = 30 + 7 = 37.
Split it into tens and ones: XXX = 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 and IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So XXXIX = 30 + 9 = 39.
Split it into tens and ones: XL = 50 − 10 = 40 and VI = 5 + 1 = 6. So XLVI = 40 + 6 = 46.
Split it into tens and ones: L = 50 and IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So LIV = 50 + 4 = 54.
Split it into tens and ones: LX = 50 + 10 = 60 and IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So LXIX = 60 + 9 = 69.
Split it into tens and ones: LXX = 50 + 10 + 10 = 70 and VIII = 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 8. So LXXVIII = 70 + 8 = 78.
Split it into tens and ones: LXXX = 50 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 80 and IV = 5 − 1 = 4. So LXXXIV = 80 + 4 = 84.
Split it into tens and ones: XC = 100 − 10 = 90 and II = 1 + 1 = 2. So XCII = 90 + 2 = 92.
Split it into tens and ones: XL = 50 − 10 = 40 and IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So XLIX = 40 + 9 = 49.
Split it into tens and ones: XC = 100 − 10 = 90 and V = 5. So XCV = 90 + 5 = 95.
Split it into tens and ones: XC = 100 − 10 = 90 and IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So XCIX = 90 + 9 = 99.

sets.title: Write numbers to 100 in Roman numerals

items.e: Partition 14 into 10 + 4. 10 is X and 4 is IV. So 14 = XIV.
Partition 19 into 10 + 9. 10 is X and 9 is IX. So 19 = XIX.
Partition 27 into 20 + 7. 20 is XX and 7 is VII. So 27 = XXVII.
XL = 50 − 10 = 40, so 40 = XL. XXXX is wrong: never write 4 Xs in a row.
76 = 70 + 6. LXX = 70, so the missing part is 6 = VI.
Partition 44 into 40 + 4. 40 is XL and 4 is IV. So 44 = XLIV.
Partition 47 into 40 + 7. 40 is XL and 7 is VII. So 47 = XLVII.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is not written correctly?
items.e: IIII is not correct: 4 is written IV. The others are correct: XIV = 14, XL = 40, LX = 60.
Partition 49 into 40 + 9. 40 is XL and 9 is IX. So 49 = XLIX. IL is not allowed: I can only go before V or X.
Partition 58 into 50 + 8. 50 is L and 8 is VIII. So 58 = LVIII.
38 = 30 + 8. XXX = 30, so the missing part is 8 = VIII.
Partition 66 into 60 + 6. 60 is LX and 6 is VI. So 66 = LXVI.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is not written correctly?
items.e: XXXX is not correct: 40 is written XL. The others are correct: XXX = 30, XLV = 45, XC = 90.
Partition 73 into 70 + 3. 70 is LXX and 3 is III. So 73 = LXXIII.
Partition 89 into 80 + 9. 80 is LXXX and 9 is IX. So 89 = LXXXIX.
XC = 100 − 10 = 90, so 90 = XC. LXXXX is wrong: never write 4 Xs in a row.
94 = 90 + 4. XC = 90, so the missing part is 4 = IV.
Partition 95 into 90 + 5. 90 is XC and 5 is V. So 95 = XCV. VC is not allowed: V is never put before a bigger symbol.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is not written correctly?
items.e: IL is not correct: I can only go before V or X. 49 is written XLIX. The others are correct: XLIX = 49, LI = 51, XIX = 19.
Partition 99 into 90 + 9. 90 is XC and 9 is IX. So 99 = XCIX. IC is not allowed: I can only go before V or X.

sets.title: Compare, order and calculate with Roman numerals

items.e: XL = 40 and LX = 60. 40 < 60, so XL < LX.
IX = 9 and XI = 11. 9 < 11, so IX < XI.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is the greatest?
items.e: XXIX = 29, XXXV = 35, XXXVIII = 38, XL = 40. XL is the greatest. A longer numeral is not always bigger.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is the greatest?
items.e: XL = 40, XLVIII = 48, LIV = 54, LX = 60. LX is the greatest. A longer numeral is not always bigger.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is the greatest?
items.e: LXXIX = 79, LXXXV = 85, LXXXVIII = 88, XC = 90. XC is the greatest. A longer numeral is not always bigger.

items.q: Which Roman numeral is the smallest?
items.e: VIII = 8, IX = 9, XI = 11, XII = 12. VIII is the smallest.

items.q: What comes next? XXXVI, XXXVII, XXXVIII, ?
items.e: XXXVI = 36, XXXVII = 37, XXXVIII = 38. The numbers go up in 1s. 38 + 1 = 39 = XXXIX.

items.q: What comes next? XL, L, LX, ?
items.e: XL = 40, L = 50, LX = 60. The numbers go up in 10s. 60 + 10 = 70 = LXX.

items.q: Which list is in order from smallest to largest?
items.e: XVI = 16, XIX = 19, XXI = 21. From smallest to largest: XVI, XIX, XXI.

items.q: Which list is in order from smallest to largest?
items.e: XXXV = 35, XL = 40, L = 50. From smallest to largest: XXXV, XL, L.

items.q: Work out XXIV + VI. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: XXIV = 24 and VI = 6. 24 + 6 = 30, and 30 = XXX.

items.q: Work out XV + IX. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: XV = 15 and IX = 9. 15 + 9 = 24, and 24 = XXIV.

items.q: Work out XL + X. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
Work out XXXV + XV. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
Work out L − I. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: L = 50 and I = 1. 50 − 1 = 49, and 49 = XLIX. IL is not allowed: I can only go before V or X.

items.q: Work out XC − X. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
Work out XIX + XXI. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: XIX = 19 and XXI = 21. 19 + 21 = 40, and 40 = XL. XXXX is wrong: never write 4 Xs in a row.

items.q: Work out LX − XV. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: LX = 60 and XV = 15. 60 − 15 = 45, and 45 = XLV. VL is not allowed: only I, X (and C) go before a bigger symbol, and only I before V or X.

items.q: Work out XLV + XLV. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: XLV = 45 and XLV = 45. 45 + 45 = 90, and 90 = XC. LXXXX is wrong: never write 4 Xs in a row.

items.q: Work out C − I. Give the answer in Roman numerals.
items.e: C = 100 and I = 1. 100 − 1 = 99, and 99 = XCIX. IC is not allowed: I can only go before V or X.

sets.title: Real life: clocks, kings and queens, books and Roman history

items.e: The minute hand (red) points to XII, so it is o’clock. The hour hand points to IX = 9. It is nine o’clock. Be careful: IX is 9, not 11.
The minute hand points to VI, which is half past. The hour hand is between IV (4) and V (5), so it is half past four. Be careful: IV is 4, not 6.
The minute hand points to III, which is quarter past. The hour hand has just passed XI (11), so it is quarter past eleven. Be careful: XI is 11, not 9.
The minute hand points to IX, which is quarter to. The hour hand is nearly at VIII (8), so it is quarter to eight.

items.q: On a clock with Roman numerals, the minute hand points to VI. How many minutes past the hour is it?
items.e: VI = 6. Each number on the clock is 5 minutes for the minute hand: 6 × 5 = 30 minutes. That is half past.

items.q: King Henry VIII had six wives. Which King Henry was he?
items.e: VIII = 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 8, so he was the 8th King Henry. We say “Henry the Eighth”.

items.q: Queen Elizabeth II’s father was King George VI. Which King George was he?
items.e: VI = 5 + 1 = 6. The I comes after the V, so add it. IV would be 4.

items.q: King Louis XIV of France was king for 72 years. Which King Louis was he?
items.e: XIV = X + IV = 10 + 4 = 14. The I is before the V, so it is taken away: XIV is not 16.

items.q: Charles III became king in 2022. If there is a king called Charles after him, how will his number be written?
items.e: The next Charles will be the 4th. 4 = 5 − 1 = IV. IIII is wrong, and VI is 6.

items.q: Ethan’s book has chapters numbered from I to XXIV. How many chapters are there?
items.e: XXIV = XX + IV = 20 + 4 = 24. The I before the V is taken away, so it is not 26.

items.q: Amelia has just finished Chapter XIX. What is the number of the next chapter?
items.e: XIX = 10 + 9 = 19. The next chapter is 20 = XX. XIXI is not a Roman numeral.

items.q: Lily reads chapters XII to XV of a book. How many chapters does she read?
items.e: XII = 12 and XV = 15. The chapters are 12, 13, 14 and 15: that is 4 chapters. 15 − 12 = 3 forgets to count chapter 12.

items.q: The newest film in a series is film XIV. What will the next film be?
items.e: XIV = 14, so the next film is 15. 15 = 10 + 5 = XV. You cannot just add an I to the end of XIV.

items.q: Roman soldiers of the Ninth Legion built a fortress at York. How did the Romans write nine?
items.e: 9 = 10 − 1, so put I before X: IX. XI is 11, and IIX is not allowed.

items.q: The Romans invaded Britain in the year AD 43. How do you write 43 in Roman numerals?
items.e: 43 = 40 + 3. 40 = XL (50 − 10) and 3 = III. So 43 = XLIII. LXIII would be 63.

items.q: A museum label says a Roman coin is from the year AD LXXIX, the year a volcano buried the town of Pompeii. What year is that?
items.e: Split it into tens and ones: LXX = 50 + 10 + 10 = 70 and IX = 10 − 1 = 9. So LXXIX = 70 + 9 = 79. The I before the X is taken away, so it is not 81.

items.q: Which Roman numeral stands for zero?
items.e: The Romans had no symbol for zero. Our zero came later, from India, through Arabic mathematicians.

items.q: In the number 77, the two 7s have different values. In the Roman numeral XX, what is each X worth?
items.e: Roman numerals do not use place value. X always means 10, wherever it is. XX = 10 + 10 = 20. In 77 the first 7 is worth 70 because of its place.

items.q: We need a 0 to write 50. Why do Roman numerals never need a zero?
c: Each symbol has a fixed value
Each symbol depends on its place
items.e: In 50 the 0 holds the ones place, so the 5 stays in the tens. Roman numerals have no places: L always means 50 and C always means 100, so 50 is just L, with no gap to fill.

items.q: Which number is much quicker to write with our digits than with Roman numerals?
items.e: 88 = LXXXVIII: 8 symbols. With digits it is just 2. 10 = X, 50 = L and 100 = C each need only 1 symbol.
